AnswerDetails: Real title: Pine Trees (Shōrin-zu byōbu), Hasegawa Tōhaku, c. 1595, Tokyo National Museum. Trivia: it is a pair of six-panel folding screens in ink on paper, pines half lost in mist, an expression of ma, the Japanese idea of meaningful empty space. They are said to be the first paintings of their size to show nothing but trees, and were named a National Treasure of Japan in 1952.
